semantic.justification: Original weak.hxx inline acquire(nonnull OWeakObject*) and borrowed getXWeak including null; OWeakObject declaration reexports the single source/weak implementation. Compiler assertion binding is explicit; no alternative weak object or type provider. V4DQJW extends the same original weak.cxx owner with non-aggregating OWeakObject and internal OWeakConnectionPoint: zero-starting actual OSL count, lazy independently acquired adapter, guard increment/rollback against resurrection, reverse pointer search then actual root identity comparison, detached ordered listener snapshot, disposed-listener handling, last RuntimeException selection, weak invalidation before virtual destruction and dummy copy/assignment. Actual Reference, queryInterface, XWeak/XAdapter/XReference, Any and exception owners are reused. Synchronous browser execution replaces mutex scope; caught UNO exception values are retained directly rather than copied through the absent native C++/binary exception bridge. This preserves dynamic JS exception fields and selection, but does not certify native exception allocation/context-refcount traces, binary ABI, threads or shutdown. Ten added real-owner tests plus six existing complete native weak-helper replays cover both changed executable owners at unchanged scoped100. No new native OWeakObject capture or generic bridge parity is claimed. OWeakAggObject, WeakImplHelper, UnoComplexColor, CellColorHandler and full DOCX/XLSX model/UI workflows remain incomplete; broad parity flags stay unverified.
